reachable: Yes, fully reachable at the scored read position, and I confirmed it by execution rather than by reading. (a) The freeze fires well inside the budget: make_target is called once per training step on tgt[cmd_mask]; with bs=64 and ~30 commands per sequence that is ~1900 rows/step, so the 20000-row floor is cleared by step 11 and the freeze triggers at call 200 of 4000. An end-to-end run of the real genome through evolve/harness.py:_train (205 steps, MPS) gave ready=1.0, dead=0.0, calls=200, rows=358924, cond(W)=26.3 on standardized data. (b) The scored path does route through to_obs: eval/adapter.py:198 takes an unregistered CPU deepcopy of net.target_module and hands it to cups_ca.measure_trained_net; cups_probe.measure:275, exposure_swap:405 and alt_chain:609 all apply target_mod.to_obs to the read-position prediction before the N-way argmin. _fwd_pred returns CPU tensors, so the CPU-only tmod and the whitening matmul are device-compatible — I ran the exact adapter sequence and it works. The author's failure-mode 4 ("the one assumption I cannot check from inside the jail") is therefore TRUE as assumed. (c) Gradient: the target is a constant (no_grad + detach), which is correct; changing it changes the loss geometry and hence every gradient in the trunk. Nothing here is gated on an observation being present, so nothing is switched off at the read. Worth recording: eval/guard_reach.py calls make_target exactly once, so `ready` stays 0 there and the gate exercised only the identity fallback — before my run, the frozen whitening branch had never executed anywhere.
solves_outside_model: No. Neither module parses command text, path strings, or move chains. The target consumes only z_obs (the standardized next-observation embeddings the harness hands it), reduces them to one global mean vector and one global 768x768 second moment, and freezes a single symmetric linear map applied identically to every row. At scoring time only to_obs runs — make_target is never called on the scored split, and the copy in the probe is a deepcopy, so the scored split cannot even contribute to the statistics. Because the same frozen W and mu are applied to every window and to both the native and the role-swapped arm, the transform cannot carry routing information and cannot create a per-window native/swap differential by itself; it can only change what the trained trunk learned. This is nothing like the retracted stream shortcut: no resolved identity ever reaches the model as input. The objective likewise reads only (pred, tgt) and takes no ctx.
summary: The code implements the described mechanism faithfully and the author's arithmetic is unusually well checked. The target axis is exactly a ridge-ZCA whitening with a variance-preserving gain: I reproduced all three quoted spectral figures to the digit (power-law exponent 1.0: eigenvalue ratio 768 -> per-direction loss-weight ratio 4.589, cond(W)=12.94; exponent 1.5: 2.128e4 -> 36.14, cond 24.27; exponent 2.0: 5.898e5 -> 631.5, cond 30.56; mean per-direction variance 1.000000 in all three), and the round-trip figure (1.49e-08 at 768d, cond 24.3). The gain formula in code matches the stated condition mean(g^2 lam/(lam+eps)) = mean(lam) exactly. W is symmetric to bit-exactness. The objective is exactly the parent r12 with the per-dimension inverse-residual precision weights deleted and _ANCHOR 0.05 replaced by _MSE_W 1.0; ring, focal and gated-repulsion blocks are character-identical. The installed chunks are byte-identical to the round directory. Fail-safe behaviour is as claimed: identity before the freeze and identity forever on any numerical failure. Reachable at the scored position and clean on the outside-the-model question. Two things do not hold up. First and most serious: the empirical premise the author explicitly labels "verified in evolve/jail_data/train_sample.jsonl" — that sibling contents on one board have "the same shape" and differ only in low-variance directions — is contradicted by that file. Boards deliberately mix INI, JSON, shell-script, CSV, unit-config and syslog formats among the siblings, and render_obs embeds the full output, so siblings differ along what is plausibly a dominant corpus direction. That is the author's own failure mode 1, asserted away with a citation that says the opposite. Second, the hypothesis treats the transform as pure loss re-weighting, but the retained r18/r22 arch and r3 head produce the prediction largely by copying raw observation tokens through diagonal-only gates (FiLM gamma/shift, out_scale), and both aux losses still supervise those reads against raw obs; after step 200 the auxiliaries and the main loss are optimizing in two different spaces. Not fatal, not a shortcut, but the archived description over-claims what the mechanism does and under-states what it disturbs. Separately worth noting for the archive, not a divergence: the target axis already contains zca_shrunk_target_whitening and r2_shrunk_zca_content_metric, so the whitening family is not new to the search even though it is new relative to this parent and partner. WHAT I COULD NOT CHECK: no encoded pack roots exist on this machine (TWM_CUPS_ROOT unset, no emb-seq-*.pt anywhere), so I could not measure the real observation-embedding spectrum, could not test whether the sibling-difference subspace is high- or low-variance in the true frame, and could not run the actual eval. My end-to-end run used guard_reach's synthetic boards, so the cond(W)=26 figure is indicative, not the real one. I also could not reproduce the "objective value 9.91 -> 8.68" figure exactly (the prediction draw is unspecified); my analogous run gave 8.12 -> 6.44, same direction and same regime.

divergences.claim: "Sibling contents on one board are all `cat` of a small config-like file on the same image at the same cwd (verified in evolve/jail_data/train_sample.jsonl: cups_expose / cups_test steps are cat of files with the same shape and differing canary strings). Their embeddings therefore agree on the dominant directions — the format, verb, image and cwd directions — and differ only in low-variance directions."
divergences.what_the_code_does: The cited file contradicts this. Within a single trajectory the cups_expose contents on one board are deliberately in DIFFERENT formats, not the same shape. seq_idx=181 exposes, on one board: an INI/KEY=VALUE file, a JSON object, a `#!/bin/sh` script, a `[unit_...]` unit-config, and a syslog-style line. seq_idx=300 exposes INI, JSON, shell, CSV and unit-config. realenv/seq_worldmodel.py:render_obs puts the full (2000-char-capped) output into the observation text, so format is fully present in the encoding, not stripped. The single premise on which the whole causal story rests — that the discriminative subspace between siblings is LOW-variance — is asserted as verified and is contradicted by the data the author cites as verification. If format is a dominant corpus direction, ridge-ZCA whitening damps exactly the subspace the score depends on, which is the author's own failure mode 1 with the sign of the effect flipped.

divergences.claim: "The prediction of the trunk plus the parent's rename-registry read is then trained under a metric in which getting the identity of the content right is most of the loss" / "no change to the forward pass of the model".
divergences.what_the_code_does: The forward pass is literally unchanged, but the target transform is not metric-only: the retained arch and head deliver the prediction largely by COPYING raw observation tokens into it, and W mixes dimensions, so those copy paths can no longer be correct. evolve/chunks/arch/r18_pathstate_latent_transition_worldmodel.py builds `pred_cmd = head(h) + sigmoid(direct_gate)*target_read + tr_contrib` where `target_read` is a softmax mixture of r_view (a FiLM'd retrieved raw obs token, gamma/shift are per-dimension only), read_path (a retrieved raw obs token) and prev_obs (the literal previous obs token). The head adds `contrib = rgate * reads * out_scale` where out_scale is a per-dimension vector and `reads` are raw obs vectors read out of the registry. A diagonal FiLM and a diagonal out_scale cannot express a dimension-mixing symmetric W. Worse, the head's aux still supervises the registry read against RAW obs tokens (InfoNCE + MSE on `o = tok[:,1::2]`, r3 head aux_loss), and the arch's transition-consistency aux likewise, so after the freeze at step 200 the auxiliary losses pull the registry read toward the raw space while the main loss requires the merged prediction to live in the whitened space. This second-order consequence is absent from the hypothesis and from its four failure modes.

divergences.claim: "The partner's contribution kept here is plain MSE at full weight ... which is stated in the same squared-L2 variable the eval decides in."
divergences.what_the_code_does: After the freeze the MSE term `((pred - tgt)**2).mean()` is computed in the WHITENED space, while the eval's decision (cups_probe._nway) is a squared-L2 in the untransformed observation space after to_obs. Those are different metrics by construction — that difference is the whole point of the candidate. The sentence contradicts the design it is describing.
divergences.evidence: evolve/chunks/objective/whitened_metric_ring_mse.py:36 vs evolve/cups_probe.py:275-276 (`pred_obs = target_mod.to_obs(...)` then `_nway` on plain squared-L2 over candidates).

divergences.claim: "Measured standalone at 1600x768 in float64 on CPU: 11.8 ms per call."
divergences.what_the_code_does: I measured the actual module's post-freeze make_target at 1600x768 float64 on CPU at 2.92 ms/call — the claim overestimates by ~4x, so its conclusion ("under a minute added to a 4000-step run") holds with margin. Separately, `_work_dtype` returns float64 on CUDA, so on the GPU lane this is an fp64 matmul; on consumer-class cards fp64 runs at 1/32-1/64 of fp32, so "far less on the GPU lane" is not guaranteed, though the absolute cost stays a few ms/step.

divergences.claim: "to_obs(make_target(z)) recovers z to a relative error ... 1.5e-8 at 768 dims on a power-law-1.5 spectrum with cond(W)=24."
divergences.what_the_code_does: Reproduces exactly on the float64 path: I measured cond(W)=24.32 and round-trip relative error 1.49e-08 at 768 dims on a power-law-1.5 spectrum. On the MPS lane _work_dtype forces float32 and the real measured round-trip error rises to 6.3e-07 on real-shaped targets — still ~6 orders below anything that could move an N-way pick, and the hypothesis does flag the MPS float32 limitation, but the quoted figures are the float64 ones only.
